audio_role: Upbeat funk instrumental with drums, bass and brass hits, no voice, no sizzle. The first 6 fast cuts land on drum hits. The middle beauty shots hold longer and sit inside the groove. Ends on a hit under the logo.
can_make: We can make the second half, not the first. From one real overhead menu photo of the set we can make shots 7-12: crops for macro and close, plus 4 s AI clips started from that photo for slow push-in and slow orbit, then cut to the beat and add the end logo. We cannot make shots 1-6 truthfully: real chopsticks putting down one roll after another with correct weight, shadow and no morphing. AI hands with chopsticks warp, and stills cut together look like a jump, not a placement. House cast not needed here; original is hands-only and we should keep it hands-only, no model holding or eating.
core: An empty plate fills piece by piece until it is full.
dish: Salmon uramaki set, 7 cut rolls with salmon-tuna filling, avocado slices outside, topped alternately with white sauce with tobiko and green oil, and with red shredded garnish.
fits: Counted small pieces served as a set where two looks alternate: sushi rolls, hosomaki, dumplings, gyoza, mini tacos, bruschetta, sweets like mochi or petit fours.
hook: In the first 0.8 s chopsticks carry a cut salmon roll in close-up and lower it onto crossed sticks over an empty glazed plate.
needs_camera: Real chopstick placement on the real plate: the grip, the release, the roll settling without wobble, true gloss on salmon and sauce, true shallow focus shift between rolls, and consistent color and size of all 7 pieces across cuts.
people: hands only. An out-of-frame hand holds wooden chopsticks, enters from left or right, places one roll per cut, then exits. No face, no body, no talking, no eating.

why_it_works: You see orange salmon centers cut open, white rice, green avocado, white sauce dots and red shreds on a green-brown plate. Each 0.8 s cut adds one piece, so the count grows 1 to 7. Close focus shows oil shine and rice grains and tobiko beads. The repetition tells portion size without words.
